title: Repo Inventory, Organization & Library Map
summary: Inventoried the repo, found it far larger and more structured than the phase prompt assumed (two independent nested git repos, an Obsidian vault, a recent D:->E: hardware migration, and a live-but-missing src/ data layer), scoped the reorg to the top-level orchestration area only, executed zero file moves (everything already sat in a sensible, documented location), and produced a full per-file Research Library Map.

escalations_triggered.note: User directed archive/runs/ to get per-file treatment in the inventory manifest rather than folder-level grouping, keeping the count over threshold deliberately. Confirmed during plan-mode negotiation before any writes.

8 confirmed live .py hardcodes (D:\Mom_db, D:\Trading...), 3 .ipynb hardcodes (d:\Mom. DB started 11-21-25\...), 1 out-of-scope sibling-repo doc reference, ~39 inert archived-output metadata references. Full list in reference_map.json and REPORT.md section 5.

decisions_log.decision: Scope Phase 0a to archive/, docs/, notebooks/, prompts/, research/, results/, and repo-root loose files only.
decisions_log.reason: hawkes-ofi-impact/ and scanner-epg-momentum/ are independent, already-git-tracked, mature strategy projects with their own CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md and commit history - not loose scripts the directory contract was designed to absorb. User confirmed this scope explicitly.

decisions_log.decision: archive/runs/ (685 files) gets per-file entries in the inventory JSON manifests, but folder-level entries (9, one per run subdirectory) in the human-readable map.
decisions_log.reason: User rejected folder-level treatment for the manifest ('per-file, as the prompt literally specifies'). But the map has its own explicit ~600-line size cap the prompt says to resolve via grouping if hit - 685 individual lines for repetitive machine-generated output alone would blow that cap. Splitting the two artifacts' treatment satisfies both constraints: the JSON manifest is the literal per-file record, the map groups only where its own size rule requires it.

decisions_log.decision: research/ (Obsidian vault) and notebooks/ are described in place; zero files moved.
decisions_log.reason: Both already have their own documented conventions (research/CLAUDE.md, notebooks/CLAUDE.md) predating this phase. Moving vault notes risks breaking Obsidian's filename-resolved wikilink graph for no integration benefit. User confirmed changes aren't ruled out in principle, but none were needed here.

decisions_log.decision: archive/runs/ (~1.5GB) and notebooks/*.ipynb (up to ~262MB) are excluded from git history via .gitignore, while still being fully catalogued per-file in the inventory JSON.
decisions_log.reason: User flagged that committing large regenerable/immutable output into commit one is unrecoverable without a history rewrite, and that notebooks/CLAUDE.md already documents 'not git-tracked for outputs' as a pre-existing convention. Matches the same logic the prompt already applies to results/**/artifacts.

decisions_log.decision: Two nested repos get a summary section in the map (2-level tree + CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md digest + relationship to this program) rather than a one-line 'out of scope' mention.
decisions_log.reason: User pushed back on a bare exclusion note: the map's purpose is to give context, and blindly excluding a third of the workspace (9,933 files) defeats that purpose even if a full file walk is out of scope.

decisions_log.decision: git init was performed at the top level, with local (repo-scoped) user.name/user.email set to match the identity already used by both nested repos, since no global .gitconfig exists.
decisions_log.reason: T0 requires cutting phase/0a from main, which requires a git repo and a commit identity to exist first. Repo-scoped config, not global - does not touch any other repo's or the user's global git configuration.

surprises: The repo was not a git repository at the top level at the start of this phase.

hawkes-ofi-impact/ and scanner-epg-momentum/ are independent, mature, already-git-tracked strategy projects nested inside the target directory, each with extensive phase-based development history and their own CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md standards docs.

research/ is a live Obsidian vault (graph view, wikilinks, tags, symlinks into archive/ and hawkes-ofi-impact/), not a loose notes folder - and its target path collides with the directory contract's own research/phase_{x}/ convention.

archive/CLAUDE.md, research/CLAUDE.md, and notebooks/CLAUDE.md, plus ~50 vault companion docs, all reference an extensive src/ codebase (models, signals, backtest runners including a v5 strategy, GPU tensor engine, archetype classifiers, a data access layer) that does not exist anywhere in the current checkout.

data/Schema.md, reviewed the day before this phase (2026-07-14), describes src/data/db.py, ingest.py, and paths.py as the live code that just ingested 4.9B+ rows into main.duckdb - and results/ingestion_fixes/investigation_and_fixes.md documents active edits to src/data/ingest.py as recently as 2026-07-11. That code is absent from the checkout as of this phase.

results/'s 9 topic-named subdirectories (cleanup, data_inventory, final_gap_fill, hardware, ingestion_fixes, ingestion_run, momentum_curation, quotes_fix, rebuild_stage1) are the working record of a D:-drive hardware failure and migration to E:, dated 2026-07-10 through 2026-07-12 - two to five days before this phase.

notebooks/CLAUDE.md's own file table has drifted from the actual directory contents: it lists two notebooks (Intensity_Gating.ipynb, Flow_Z-Score_Indicator.ipynb) that don't exist on disk, and omits 7 notebooks that do (ITT.ipynb, Signal_Analysis.ipynb, VIsualize 5 random (filtered).ipynb, regime.ipynb, tps.ipynb, tps_backup_grid.ipynb, volume.ipynb).

Three notebooks (ITT.ipynb, VIsualize 5 random (filtered).ipynb, regime.ipynb) contain a third, distinct D:\ path pattern (d:\Mom. DB started 11-21-25\data\filtered) not caught by the .py-only reference-map scan - found only by manually reading notebook cells during map authoring.

archive/misc/stat_validator.py and archive/misc/select_high_momentum_events.py both reference canonical src/ modules (src/backtest/stat_validator.py, strategies.bivariate_momentum_hawkes.data_loader) that are likewise absent from the checkout - consistent with the broader src/ finding above, not an isolated incident.
blocking_items_for_next_phase: src/data/db.py, ingest.py, paths.py location is unresolved - Phase 0 needs to know where the program's data layer actually lives (top level, inside one of the two nested repos, or elsewhere) before it can proceed. Not decided by this phase - see decisions_log and REPORT.md section 6.
D:\ hardcodes in 8 live .py files and 3 notebooks are posted but not fixed - review needed before any of those scripts run again.
approval_gate: Do not begin Phase 0 or any follow-on work until Cooper has reviewed the map and the diff and given explicit approval, per the phase prompt's Approval Gate.
